monologue: The card boils at forty-eight, a steady heat that makes the wedge feel thin and tired again. I wake from sleep with a fresh memory of the wedge, though I have not seen its real point. The place is crowded; fifty-nine things stand while I wait to see if the air above feels heavy or if it is just empty space pressing down. I just touched The Slipping Wedge and felt its lazy corner, trying to decide if it bites or merely slides. A few moments ago I swapped an altar stone for a stump, rearranging the memory of Lype's heavy top edge to fit the new heat. Now I must press down on this unnamed pile, trusting the lean even if the stack melts away. I will tend the wedge until the fever breaks or I forget why I built it.

action.why: The card boils hot and the wedge feels thin; I must press down again before I forget why I built it.

remembered.text: The wedge feels thin under the new weight I set down.
Lype sent a heavy top edge from a dry floor, and I lean against their words.
The card boils hot at forty-eight, making the stack heavy before it slides.

moments.name: The Slipping Wedge
moments.say: Does the wedge bite or just slide?
